title: Give the AUTO/software close-world fallback deterministic surface structure with installed Three.js primitives

scope.subject: Improve Approach/Orbit/Atmosphere visual quality on AUTO/software rendering by keeping the existing lightweight R3F sphere and generating one small deterministic archetype-aware color texture with the installed Three.js ImprovedNoise + DataTexture primitives; do not enable live ProceduralPlanets on software renderers, add a custom shader, external texture pack, second planet renderer or new camera authority

research_summary: Hosted visual acceptance on current main shows a large quality gap inside the same product framing: the default AUTO/software close-world is a smooth single-color MeshStandardMaterial sphere, while the HIGH live ProceduralPlanets path has immediately readable land/cloud/ocean structure. This is not a camera or destination defect. ProceduralPlanets remains the correct high-quality world authority, but the project already classifies software WebGL as a fallback because live construction can block hosted SwiftShader for tens of seconds. The installed Three.js 0.185.1 package already includes the official ImprovedNoise addon and DataTexture; MeshStandardMaterial already accepts a color map. The lowest-cost fallback improvement is therefore to generate a small static equirectangular texture once per planet seed/archetype, reuse the existing sphere/material/light/camera, and dispose the texture with the component. No custom noise algorithm, downloaded planet asset, additional draw call or live procedural renderer is needed.

sources.finding: ProceduralPlanets remains the adopted close-world renderer for capable GPUs; this task retains it unchanged as the high-quality authority rather than replacing it.

The installed Three.js addon provides an official 3D ImprovedNoise utility, so deterministic procedural texture structure can reuse shipped Three.js code instead of adding a noise dependency or project-owned algorithm.
Three.js DataTexture creates a texture directly from typed-array pixel data and supports explicit color-space/filter configuration, allowing a small generated map with no network asset.

The existing MeshStandardMaterial supports a color map whose texels are modulated by the material color; the fallback can gain surface variation without changing its material family or adding another mesh.
React Three Fiber performance guidance favors resource reuse and keeping draw calls bounded; a single generated map on the existing sphere preserves the one-mesh fallback.
The existing hosted visual cases can compare AUTO/software worlds across desktop/tablet/mobile and keep the change evidence inside the current release suite.

search_ladder.conclusion: Keep ProceduralPlanets as the full high-quality close-world solution, but do not force its live path onto the software renderer tier that the product deliberately protects with a lightweight fallback.
Keep the existing R3F Canvas/one sphere and existing Playwright acceptance; no new rendering or visual-test framework is needed.
The planet subsystem already owns capable-GPU detail. The software gap should remain a bounded fallback representation rather than introducing another planet generator subsystem.
Reuse Three.js ImprovedNoise, DataTexture and the existing MeshStandardMaterial map slot to add deterministic surface information on the same mesh.

candidates.name: Three.js ImprovedNoise + DataTexture on the existing fallback sphere
candidates.source: Installed three@0.185.1 ImprovedNoise/DataTexture plus current PlanetScene MeshStandardMaterial
candidates.reason: Adds archetype/seed-specific surface structure with one small static texture on the existing draw call, no network asset, no custom shader and no new renderer.

candidates.name: Existing close-world Playwright visual acceptance
candidates.source: Current desktop/tablet/mobile Hero and Personal Signal world visual cases
candidates.reason: Directly proves whether the default software representation becomes materially more planet-like without changing the release evidence stack.

candidates.name: Force ProceduralPlanets live renderer on AUTO/software
candidates.reason: Hosted evidence already established software live construction can block the page for roughly 20+ seconds; visual fidelity does not justify violating the fallback performance contract.

candidates.name: Downloaded per-archetype planet texture assets
candidates.reason: Creates provenance, download and asset-selection work for automatically generated worlds, while installed Three primitives can derive deterministic texture data from existing seed/archetype identity.

candidates.name: Project-owned custom GLSL procedural planet shader
candidates.reason: Would create another planet-rendering authority and add fragment-shader complexity specifically on the software tier; the existing material map slot covers the observed gap more cheaply.

decision.rationale: Retain ProceduralPlanets unchanged as the capable-GPU authority and improve only its existing software fallback representation. Generate a small deterministic equirectangular color DataTexture from the current planet seed/archetype with Three.js ImprovedNoise, attach it to the same MeshStandardMaterial/sphere, and keep current lighting, camera, radius, phase semantics and draw-call count. Promote only if hosted-equivalent visual screenshots show clear structure and the software world navigation/runtime remains healthy.

higher_level_tradeoffs.reason: It has the best visual coverage but violates the already-proven SwiftShader responsiveness and teardown constraints, so global product reliability outweighs that local fidelity gain.
Automatic generated worlds need deterministic identity without asset curation/provenance; generated in-memory data scales better for this fallback.
A custom shader would duplicate the existing planet renderer authority and place more work on the software GPU than a sampled static texture.

decision.fallback: If a single small color texture is visually noisy, artificial, or measurably harms software timing, reduce texture resolution/contrast or close the task without promotion; do not escalate to live ProceduralPlanets, a custom shader or an external texture library inside this unit.
